title: Observability library modernization and sampling/rate-limit performance cleanup
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Goal: Reduce p99 observability overhead and improve signal fidelity by modernizing our tracing and logging libraries across the runtime and gateway services. Scope: (1) Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK to latest stable release and migrate from in-house shim to upstream semantic conventions; (2) Replace legacy logging wrapper with structured JSON logger (compatible with our central ingest); (3) Implement adaptive sampling and coordinated rate-limit hooks to reduce burst CPU in high-throughput tails; (4) Standardize metric naming and delta-counters to avoid cardinality explosion. Out of scope: agent-side end-to-end tracing of third-party adapters (followup ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK across runtime and gateway without losing existing trace continuity (traces keep same trace IDs for existing services)
CPU overhead attributable to observability on p99 requests reduced by >= 35% in synthetic high-throughput test
Logs emitted in structured JSON format with required fields (service, env, trace_id, span_id, severity, message)
Adaptive sampling toggles exposed via runtime flags and Console feature flagging for rollout
No increase in production error rates attributable to library changes; automated canary validates end-to-end flows
test_plan: Unit tests for new logger adapter and OTEL exporter; integration test harness using local replay of production traces; load test scenario (k6 + internal trace-generator) that reproduces prior high-throughput incident; canary and synthetic SLO checks (latency and error rate) in staging before progressive rollout to prod regions.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branches behind runtime feature flag; 2) Deploy gateway and runtime in staging with sampling set to conservative (1%); 3) Run canonical load tests and validate dashboards; 4) Enable canary for 5% traffic in us-west-2 for 24 hours; 5) Ramp to 25% then 100% over 48-72 hours with health gates; 6) After full rollout, switch adaptive sampler to default policy and monitor for 7 days.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Priya: Initial triage of scope complete. Identified 3 hotspots: legacy logging adapter, blocking exporter flush on shutdown, and a coarse-grained rate limiter in request preprocessing.

2026-02-18 - Miguel: Prototype of structured logger done; emits required fields and passes unit tests. Opening PR to runtime (see PR #2387). Notes: performance comparable to current logger at low concurrency but ~12% faster under moderate load.

2026-02-25 - SRE (Aisha): Load test reproducing incident showed exporter flush blocking adds ~18ms per-request at p99. Proposal: switch to async batch exporter and add backpressure signals to sampler.
2026-03-02 - Design review: Decided to adopt OpenTelemetry semantic conventions v1.12 and keep our extra labels under 'redwood.*' to avoid upstream collisions. Design approved by @Tom (PM).

2026-03-05 - Miguel: Integrated adaptive sampler + local rate-limit hook. Found edge-case with long-running streaming requests where sampling decision was lost; added span attribute persisting logic. New integration tests added.
2026-03-09 - Security review note (internal): Confirmed no PII added to spans/logs; masking retained for prompt text fields. No additional KMS integration required for observability data.
2026-03-12 - Miguel: Canary config prepared. Staging run shows CPU observability overhead down 40% on p99 for runtime service. Preparing canary rollout notes and monitoring runbooks.
